metadata.description: Taxation analysis for Bangladeshi CS/AI/ML students and graduates across target countries, covering student phase, post-study work, and settled professional phases
metadata.targetProfile: Bangladeshi student/graduate, CS/AI/ML field, age 22-32, planning 2027-2029 intake
metadata.criticalNote: Tax burden directly determines net savings and PR timeline speed. A country with 40% tax but zero tuition may yield better net outcome than a country with 25% tax and USD 40,000 tuition. Always calculate NET after-tax savings, not gross salary.
metadata.bangladeshDoubleTaxNote: Bangladesh has Double Taxation Avoidance Agreements (DTAA) with several countries including Germany, Japan, South Korea, China, France. This prevents being taxed twice on the same income. Students should register as non-resident in Bangladesh to avoid dual tax obligations.

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Students on study permit become Canadian tax residents from Day 1; must file annual T1 return
studentPhase.tuitionTaxCredit: Tuition fees generate non-refundable tax credits (15% federal); carry forward unused credits
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: TA/RA stipends fully taxable as employment income; scholarships/bursaries partially exempt up to education amount
studentPhase.effectiveTaxOnStipend: Typically 0-10% effective rate on CAD 20,000-30,000 annual stipend due to basic personal amount (CAD 15,705 tax-free 2026)

workingGraduatePhase.provincialTax: Add 6-17% provincial tax on top of federal; Ontario 5.05-13.16%; Quebec 14-25.75%; Alberta 10% flat (lowest)
workingGraduatePhase.cpp: Canada Pension Plan: 5.95% employee contribution up to CAD 73,200 earnings
workingGraduatePhase.ei: Employment Insurance: 1.66% up to CAD 63,200 insurable earnings
workingGraduatePhase.albertaAdvantage: Alberta has no provincial sales tax and lowest provincial income tax; Calgary tech scene growing; meaningful advantage

taxTreaty.note: No Canada-Bangladesh DTAA; file as non-resident in Bangladesh to avoid dual filing

taxation.gstHst: 5-15% on goods/services depending on province; Ontario 13% HST; Alberta 5% GST only
taxation.capitalGainsTax: 50% inclusion rate on capital gains (proposed increase to 67% for gains over CAD 250,000 in 2025 budget; monitor)
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: April 30 annually; June 15 for self-employed
taxation.recommendation: Alberta (Calgary/Edmonton) offers lowest total tax burden. Quebec offers generous family benefits offsetting higher taxes. Tax burden is significant but manageable with RRSP optimization.

taxation.taxSystemType: Progressive federal; no separate state income tax

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Students residing 6+ months become Australian tax residents; must lodge annual tax return
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: RTP scholarship stipend is TAX-FREE (exempt from income tax under ITAA 1997); major advantage
studentPhase.partTimeWorkTax: Part-time earnings taxed at standard rates; first AUD 18,200 tax-free (tax-free threshold)
studentPhase.tfn: Tax File Number (TFN) required; without TFN employer withholds 47% - get TFN immediately on arrival

workingGraduatePhase.medicareLevy: 2% Medicare Levy on all taxable income (covers public healthcare access)
workingGraduatePhase.superannuation: 11.5% employer contribution to superannuation (retirement fund); on top of salary; not deducted from take-home but employer cost
workingGraduatePhase.helpDebt: HECS-HELP debt for domestic students; international students pay upfront; no HELP debt for international students

taxTreaty.note: No Australia-Bangladesh DTAA; file as non-resident in Bangladesh

taxation.gst: 10% GST on most goods and services
taxation.superannuationNote: Superannuation 11.5% employer contribution is effectively deferred salary; accessible at preservation age (60); departing Australia superannuation payment (DASP) available when leaving permanently (35% tax on withdrawal for temporary residents)
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: October 31 (self-lodge) or May 15 via registered tax agent
taxation.recommendation: RTP PhD stipend tax-free status is a significant advantage. Effective tax rates moderate by developed world standards. Superannuation is bonus savings. Medicare Levy buys healthcare access.

taxation.taxSystemType: Progressive federal; church tax optional; solidarity surcharge reduced

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Students with Anmeldung (registration) are German tax residents; tax return mandatory if any taxable income
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: DAAD and DFG scholarships up to EUR 934/month: TAX-FREE; PhD employment contract (TVöD) salary is fully taxable
studentPhase.hiwi: Student HiWi (Hilfswissenschaftler) earnings taxed; but Minijob under EUR 556/month is tax-free
studentPhase.taxClassNote: Tax Class 1 for single unmarried; register at Finanzamt with Steueridentifikationsnummer
studentPhase.annualRefund: Students often receive significant tax refund (Steuererstattung) due to education expenses; file Einkommensteuererklärung via ELSTER or Wundertax

workingGraduatePhase.solidaritySurcharge: Soli abolished for most taxpayers since 2021; applies above EUR 18,130 annual tax liability only
workingGraduatePhase.churchTax: 8-9% of income tax if registered with church; register as 'keine Konfession' (no denomination) to avoid

socialContributions.healthInsurance: 7.3% employee share (+ 1.7% average Zusatzbeitrag) = approximately 9% of gross

effectiveTaxRate.salary55k: Approximately 38-42% combined income tax + social contributions
effectiveTaxRate.note: Germany's high gross-to-net deduction is the most significant financial planning factor

taxTreaty.treatyNote: Germany-Bangladesh DTAA signed; prevents double taxation on employment income; file Ansässigkeitsbescheinigung if needed

taxation.vat: 19% standard VAT; 7% reduced rate on food, books, public transport
keyDeductions: Homeoffice Pauschale EUR 6/day up to EUR 1,260/year
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: July 31 (self-lodge); November 30 (via Steuerberater/ELSTER)
taxation.bluecardTaxNote: EU Blue Card holders file as regular tax residents; no special expatriate tax regime unlike Netherlands
taxation.recommendation: Germany has Europe's highest tax+social contribution burden. Net salary significantly lower than gross. However zero tuition during study phase compensates massively. Optimize with Steuerberater (tax advisor) annually - typical refund EUR 1,000-3,000 for PhD students.

taxation.taxSystemType: Progressive; PAYE system; USC and PRSI additional

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Present 183+ days in Ireland = tax resident
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: IRC/SFI research grants exempt from income tax (Income Tax Act exemption for bona fide research); TA income is taxable
studentPhase.ppsNumber: PPS Number required for employment and tax; apply at Intreo centre

workingGraduatePhase.prsi: Pay Related Social Insurance (PRSI): 4% employee on most earnings

effectiveTaxRate.salary60k: Approximately 35-38% combined income tax + USC + PRSI

taxation.vat: 23% standard; 13.5% reduced; 0% on food and children's clothing
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: October 31 (self-assessment); PAYE workers can claim via myAccount.revenue.ie
taxation.recommendation: Ireland's tax is high especially above EUR 42k where 40% rate kicks in immediately. USC adds further burden. However major US tech companies have Irish headquarters meaning access to ESOP/RSU compensation which can significantly supplement salary.

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Register at gemeente → automatic BSN (tax number) → tax resident
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: NWO PhD employment salary fully taxable; student grants/scholarships generally exempt
studentPhase.zorgtoeslag: Healthcare allowance (zorgtoeslag) available for low-income residents; approximately EUR 135/month subsidy

workingGraduatePhase.socialContributions: Partially included in Box 1 rate above; AOW pension, healthcare

thirtyPercentRuling.description: 30% of gross salary paid as tax-free expatriate allowance; dramatically reduces effective tax rate
thirtyPercentRuling.eligibility: Recruited from abroad with specific expertise; salary above EUR 46,107 (2026 threshold); application within 4 months of start
thirtyPercentRuling.impact: Effective tax rate on EUR 80,000 salary drops from approximately 38% to approximately 26% with 30% ruling
thirtyPercentRuling.bangladeshiApplicability: Highly applicable for PhD graduates entering Dutch tech market from abroad; negotiate 30% ruling in employment contract

taxation.vat: 21% standard; 9% reduced on food, medicines, books

boxSystem.box1: Employment and home ownership income; progressive 36.97-49.5%
boxSystem.box3: Savings and investments; deemed return taxation; 36% on deemed 6.17% return on wealth above EUR 57,000

taxation.taxFilingDeadline: May 1 via Belastingdienst.nl; extension possible to September
taxation.recommendation: 30% ruling is THE critical tax optimization for Bangladeshi PhD graduates entering Dutch tech market. With 30% ruling, Netherlands becomes one of Europe's most tax-efficient destinations for skilled workers. Ensure employer applies for 30% ruling within 4 months of employment start.

taxation.taxSystemType: Progressive municipal + state income tax; among world's highest

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Register at Skatteverket with personnummer; tax resident from registration
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: Doktorand (PhD employee) salary fully taxable; SI scholarship partly exempt (living allowance taxable in Sweden)
studentPhase.municipalTax: Municipal tax approximately 32% on all income above SEK 24,238 (basic deduction 2026)

incomeTaxStructure.municipalTax: Approximately 32% (varies by municipality; Stockholm 29.83%; varies nationally 29-35%)
incomeTaxStructure.stateTax: 20% additional on income above SEK 615,300 (approximately USD 59,000)

workingGraduatePhase.employerSocialContributions: 31.42% of gross salary paid by employer (not deducted from employee salary but total employer cost)

taxation.vat: 25% standard; 12% on food and hotels; 6% on books and public transport

expertTaxRelief.description: Expert Tax Relief (Expertskatt): 25% of salary tax-free for 5 years for qualifying foreign experts
expertTaxRelief.eligibility: Monthly salary above SEK 112,900 (2026) OR specific expert classification
expertTaxRelief.bangladeshiApplicability: Senior AI/ML engineers may qualify; apply through employer
expertTaxRelief.impact: Effective tax rate drops from 32% to approximately 22% on qualifying salary

taxation.socialBenefits: High tax funds: free healthcare, free university education, subsidized childcare (maxTaxa max SEK 1,572/month/child), 480 days parental leave at 80% salary
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: May 2 via Skatteverket app (very streamlined; pre-filled digital return)
taxation.recommendation: Sweden has among Europe's highest marginal tax but comprehensive social benefits in return. Expert Tax Relief applicable for senior AI engineers. Net salary lower than UK/Germany nominally but healthcare, childcare, and parental leave effectively add 15-20% to total compensation value. PhD doktorand income after 32% tax still livable comfortably.

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Register at Digital and Population Data Services Agency (DVV) for Finnish ID
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: Academy of Finland PhD employment salary taxable; YTHS student healthcare is free/subsidized
studentPhase.municipalTax: Municipal tax 16.5-23% depending on municipality; Helsinki 18.5%

workingGraduatePhase.municipalTax: Add 16.5-23% municipal tax on top; effectively 35-45% combined for mid-range salaries
workingGraduatePhase.socialContributions: Pension (7.15%), unemployment (1.5%), health insurance (2.04%) employee contributions

taxation.keyRelief: Key Employee Act: 32% flat tax for foreign key employees earning EUR 5,800+/month; applicable for senior AI roles; 4-year benefit
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: April-May; pre-filled return via vero.fi (very efficient digital system)
taxation.recommendation: Finland's tax burden is high but Key Employee 32% flat tax regime benefits senior AI professionals significantly. Social benefits comprehensive including world-class childcare. Aalto area Espoo municipality has one of lower municipal tax rates. VAT increase to 25.5% in 2024 notably increased cost of living.

taxation.taxSystemType: Progressive with high rates; among world's highest income tax

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Register at borger.dk for CPR number; automatic tax resident
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: PhD employment (stipend position) fully taxable from DKK 1; no tax-free threshold
studentPhase.su: Danish SU grant for domestic/EU students; not applicable for Bangladeshi students on PhD employment

incomeTaxStructure.bottomBracket: 12.01% municipal + 8% AM-bidrag (labor market) on all income
incomeTaxStructure.topBracket: Additional 15% state tax on income above DKK 588,900 (2026)
incomeTaxStructure.effective: Approximately 37-42% effective on mid-range salaries; up to 52% marginal
incomeTaxStructure.amBidrag: 8% AM-bidrag deducted first from gross; remaining subject to income tax

workingGraduatePhase.note: Despite high tax, PhD stipend DKK 36,000/month gross yields DKK 24,000-26,000 net (USD 3,504-3,796) which covers living costs well

taxation.vat: 25% on all goods and services (no reduced rate for food)

researcherTaxScheme.description: Researcher Tax Scheme: 27% flat rate for 7 years for qualifying researchers/highly paid employees
researcherTaxScheme.eligibility: Monthly salary minimum DKK 75,100 (2026); foreign researcher or employee recruited from abroad
researcherTaxScheme.bangladeshiApplicability: Highly applicable for PhD graduates entering Danish industry; significant tax savings
researcherTaxScheme.impact: 27% flat vs 40%+ standard = substantial net income improvement

taxation.taxFilingDeadline: May 1 via skat.dk (pre-filled; extremely user-friendly digital system)
taxation.recommendation: Denmark nominally highest-tax country in this list but Researcher Tax Scheme at 27% flat is transformative for AI/CS graduates. PhD salary net income is among Europe's highest in absolute terms despite high tax. Negotiate Researcher Scheme eligibility from Day 1 of employment.

taxation.taxSystemType: Progressive with moderate rates; oil-funded welfare state

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Register at Folkeregisteret for D-number then national ID number
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: NTNU Research Fellow (stipendiat) salary fully taxable; no scholarship exemption
studentPhase.startDeduction: New residents receive Personfradrag (personal deduction) NOK 88,250 tax-free

incomeTaxStructure.flatRate: 22% flat income tax on general income
incomeTaxStructure.stepTax: Additional progressive Trinnskatt on personal income

taxation.vat: 25% standard; 15% on food; 12% on transport and hotels
taxation.wealthTax: 0.85% on net wealth above NOK 1.7 million (approximately USD 162,000); notable for property owners
keyDeductions: Standard deduction (minstefradrag) 46% of income up to NOK 104,450
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: April 30 via skatteetaten.no (pre-filled; very digital)
taxation.recommendation: Norway has moderate tax rates by Scandinavian standards. Combined with world's highest PhD salary (NOK 43,100/month gross) and comprehensive benefits, net financial position is strong. Wealth tax is a consideration for long-term property holders. Oil-funded state means exceptional public service quality.

taxation.taxSystemType: Three-tier: federal + cantonal + municipal; one of world's most favorable

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Register at Einwohnerkontrolle (residents' registration office) within 8-14 days of arrival
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: ETH/EPFL PhD salary fully taxable; no special exemption
studentPhase.quellensteuer: Source tax (Quellensteuer) withheld directly by employer for non-permit C holders; automatic withholding

taxStructure.cantonalMunicipal: Varies enormously by canton; Zug 11-12%, Zurich 25-27%, Geneva 33-45%
taxStructure.totalEffective: Zurich: approximately 28-32% total; Zug: approximately 15-20% total

workingGraduatePhase.socialContributions: AHV/IV pension (5.3% employee), ALV unemployment (1.1%), total approximately 6.5% employee
workingGraduatePhase.pilarSystem: Three-pillar pension: AHV (state), BVG (occupational), private; BVG automatically enrolled by employer

taxation.vat: 8.1% standard; 3.8% hotel; 2.5% food and medicines (among Europe's lowest VAT)
taxation.lumpSumTaxation: Available for wealthy foreigners not working in Switzerland; not relevant for working AI professionals
keyDeductions: Professional expenses flat CHF 2,000 or actual
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: March 31 (cantonal variation; extensions common); via cantonal tax portal
taxation.recommendation: Switzerland offers Europe's best net salary for senior AI professionals. Low VAT, moderate income tax (especially Zurich vs Geneva), low social contributions. ETH/EPFL PhD net salary CHF 3,400+/month (USD 3,842+) covers living with savings. Live in canton Schwyz and work in Zurich for significant tax optimization (legal and common practice among Swiss professionals).

taxation.taxSystemType: Progressive federal + state income tax (varies enormously by state)

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: F-1 students are non-resident aliens for tax purposes for first 5 years; different forms and rates apply
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: PhD stipend/fellowship: first USD 5,000 may be exempt under US-Bangladesh tax treaty; remainder taxable at 14% for non-residents
studentPhase.sstaxExemption: F-1 students EXEMPT from Social Security and Medicare taxes (FICA); saves 7.65% vs residents
studentPhase.taxForms: Non-residents file Form 1040-NR; OPT/CPT workers also 1040-NR for 5 years

bangladeshTreaty.benefit: Article 21 student exemption: first USD 5,000 of fellowship/scholarship exempt from US tax for first 2 years

stateTaxVariation.note: No state income tax; Austin tech hub
No state income tax; Miami tech growing
High; NYC adds 3.876% city tax on top

workingGraduatePhase.ficaTax: Social Security 6.2% (up to USD 176,100) + Medicare 1.45% = 7.65% employee FICA
workingGraduatePhase.rsuBonusNote: Big Tech compensation includes RSU (stock grants) which are taxed as ordinary income at vesting; significant additional compensation but large tax event

taxTreaty.treatyNote: US-Bangladesh Tax Treaty: Article 21 covers students; employment income not specially treated; standard US tax applies for workers

taxation.stateTaxStrategy: Texas, Washington, Florida = zero state income tax; massive advantage for high earners; Seattle (Amazon, Microsoft) and Austin (Tesla, Apple, Oracle) are optimal locations
keyOptimizations: Maximize 401k pre-tax contribution (reduces taxable income USD 23,500)
HSA triple tax advantage if eligible HDHP plan
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: April 15 via IRS; automatic extension to October 15 available
taxation.recommendation: USA tax system highly geography-dependent. Seattle or Austin provide zero state income tax with world's highest AI salaries = maximum net savings. California's 13.3% top rate dramatically reduces savings. 401k optimization is critical. F-1 FICA exemption saves 7.65% during student/OPT phase - significant.

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Register at local ward office (shiyakusho) within 14 days; mynumber (social security number) issued
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: MEXT scholarship: national tax EXEMPT (government-designated scholarship); however resident tax may apply in second year
studentPhase.healthInsurance: Students join National Health Insurance (Kokumin Kenko Hoken); income-based premium approximately JPY 2,000-5,000/month

workingGraduatePhase.residentTax: Approximately 10% flat on previous year income (delayed one year; first year in Japan no resident tax)
workingGraduatePhase.jpyWeaknessNote: JPY has depreciated 30%+ against USD since 2021; USD-denominated value of Japan salaries significantly reduced; monitor exchange rate

taxTreaty.treatyNote: Japan-Bangladesh Tax Convention: covers employment income; prevents double taxation; students may benefit from Article on students and trainees

taxation.consumptionTax: 10% on most goods; 8% reduced on food and non-alcoholic beverages
taxation.hspTaxBenefit: Highly Skilled Professional (HSP) visa holders: special income deduction available; consult tax specialist
keyDeductions: Furusato Nozei (hometown tax donation) - significant reduction and gifts
taxation.yearEndAdjustment: Most employed workers have year-end tax adjustment (nenmatsu chosei) done by employer; simple process
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: March 15 via e-Tax or tax office; employer handles most adjustments
taxation.recommendation: MEXT scholarship tax exemption is a major advantage during study phase. Working phase tax is moderate but JPY weakness significantly reduces USD-denominated savings. Furusato Nozei is a unique Japanese tax optimization tool providing significant effective tax reduction plus regional gifts. Target foreign tech companies (Google, Amazon Japan) which pay significantly more than Japanese domestic firms.

taxation.taxSystemType: Progressive national income tax + local income tax

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Register at immigration office; foreigner registration certificate issued
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: KGSP scholarship: TAX-EXEMPT; KAIST RA stipend: taxable as earned income
studentPhase.nhis: National Health Insurance mandatory; student rate significantly subsidized approximately KRW 60,000/month

taxTreaty.treatyNote: Korea-Bangladesh Tax Treaty in force; employment income covered; prevents double taxation

foreignerFlatTax.description: Foreign workers may elect 19% flat tax rate on employment income for first 5 years
foreignerFlatTax.benefit: If effective rate would exceed 19%, flat rate is significantly lower; highly beneficial for mid-to-high earners
foreignerFlatTax.bangladeshiApplicability: Very applicable for KAIST graduates entering Samsung/Kakao/Naver; elect this option through employer at year-end

taxation.taxFilingDeadline: May 31 via Hometax (홈택스); employer typically handles year-end settlement
taxation.recommendation: Korea's flat 19% foreign worker tax option is highly valuable - elect this through employer. KGSP scholarship tax exemption excellent during study phase. Combined with relatively low cost of living, net savings potential is good. Korea-Bangladesh tax treaty prevents dual taxation.

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Foreigners residing 183+ days/year are Chinese tax residents
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: CSC scholarship stipend: TAX-EXEMPT as educational grant; university salary/RA is taxable
studentPhase.foreignerExemption: Foreign scholars' lecture/research grants may qualify for specific IIT exemptions

foreignerPreferences2026.housingAllowance: Foreign employee housing/meal/children's education allowances EXEMPT from IIT (extended to 2027)
foreignerPreferences2026.annualBonus: One-time annual bonus taxed separately at lower effective rate
foreignerPreferences2026.note: Foreign expert benefits being phased out progressively; confirm current status annually

taxTreaty.treatyNote: China-Bangladesh Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement in force; comprehensive coverage of employment income

taxation.vat: 13% standard; 9% on food, utilities, transport; 6% on services
taxation.capitalControls: SAFE regulations limit annual personal foreign currency remittance to USD 50,000; significant for repatriating savings to Bangladesh or transferring to third country
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: March 1 - June 30 annual comprehensive settlement via personal income tax app
taxation.recommendation: China's IIT rates moderate but capital controls limit USD remittance (USD 50,000/year cap). Tax-exempt CSC scholarship excellent for study phase. Foreign employee housing allowance exemption reduces effective tax significantly while it lasts. China-Bangladesh DTAA prevents double taxation. Main risk: capital controls complicate wealth transfer for future country transition.

studentPhase.tuitionTaxCredit: Course fees relief available if related to employment
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: University scholarships are generally tax exempt

workingGraduatePhase.cpp: CPF (Central Provident Fund): Only for PRs/Citizens. Foreigners pay 0% CPF.

taxation.taxFilingDeadline: April 18 (e-filing)

studentPhase.stipendTaxability: Research grants (allocations de recherche) are taxable.

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Resident if registered in national register.
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: PhD scholarships are often tax-free if they meet specific academic conditions.

workingGraduatePhase.provincialTax: Municipal tax 0-9% of the income tax due.

taxation.capitalGainsTax: 0% on normal management of private wealth (huge benefit)
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: End of June (online)
taxation.recommendation: Belgium has arguably the highest income tax burden on labor in the world. However, capital gains on stocks are entirely tax-free, and employers heavily use net allowances and company cars to offset the income tax.

studentPhase.taxResidencyNote: Resident if > 183 days.
studentPhase.stipendTaxability: Scholarships are generally exempt from income tax.

taxation.capitalGainsTax: 0% (No comprehensive CGT, bright-line test for property)
keyDeductions: Very few. NZ operates a broad-base, low-rate, no-deduction system.
taxation.taxFilingDeadline: July 7
taxation.recommendation: NZ income taxes are lower and simpler than Australia, Canada, and Europe. The lack of capital gains tax is a benefit, but salaries are also nominally much lower.

comparativeTaxSummary.strategicRecommendation: For maximum lifetime net income: USA (Texas/Seattle) for peak earnings phase → Netherlands (30% ruling) or Switzerland for European career → Canada/Australia for final settlement. Key insight: expat tax schemes in Netherlands (30% ruling), Denmark (researcher scheme), and Sweden (expert relief) make these countries significantly more tax-efficient than headline rates suggest. Always negotiate expat tax scheme eligibility on Day 1 of employment.
